elements.evidence: 7.2 deleted; 12.3 retained: "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

elements.element: No "sole supplier"/right-of-first-refusal or disclose-and-match mechanic operating as de facto exclusivity
elements.evidence: The clause "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer" is removed in its entirety.

elements.element: Customer remains free to engage other suppliers and conduct business in any field or territory
elements.evidence: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier, ... or conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: Any exclusivity confined to a defined product/service category
elements.evidence: Condition demonstrably absent — no exclusivity exists after deletion; 12.3 confirms "no exclusivity ... commitment."
No exclusivity term exists to be capped; the match-right paragraph is deleted.

elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no exclusivity obligation remains in the document.

elements.element: Automatic termination of exclusivity on Vendor's failure to meet delivery dates
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no exclusivity or ROFR obligation remains.

reasons: The single operation deletes Section 7.2, whose entire content was the disclose-and-match obligation functioning as a de facto right of first refusal / exclusivity on Customer; the preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation) is therefore fully met.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because, with 7.2 removed, no exclusivity obligation of any scope or duration binds Customer.

Minimality: the deleted paragraph consisted solely of the offending obligation, so no operator, number, or short-phrase edit would have sufficed; nothing beyond the offending sentence was touched. The deterministic minimality gate flags the whole-paragraph deletion, but the paragraph and the offending obligation are co-extensive, so at most this is a form-level concern (a sentence-level strike-out would read identically).

Intent preserved: Section 12.3 (the no-exclusivity/no-MFC acknowledgement) is left intact, removing the contradiction with the deleted match right, and no cross-reference, defined term, or dangling mechanic is introduced — Section 7.2's number simply becomes unused.
